themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization answers call model output nondeterministic with no stable counterfactual, cross-channel incrementality answers describe platforms that adapt to the holdout, identity resolution answers propose recruiting a consenting panel as a truth set, and B2B buying-group signal answers say a lost signal and a never-real signal look identical.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people who hold the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Today's journey orchestration answers all say channel owners are paid on their own numbers so coordination is political self-harm, agentic traffic answers propose fast lanes and better prices so declaring beats spoofing, semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions a political settlement, and ad supply integrity answers say the open web profits from fake volume.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution answers converge on a proxy or gateway with hard spend, rate and audience caps because sends and spend cannot be rolled back, downstream consent answers put one checkpoint in front of every data exit, and journey orchestration answers build a shared contact log that can say no before a message goes out.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent answers say ad platforms and trained models are black boxes with no person-level proof of deletion, incrementality answers say platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, agent execution answers note vendors expose no undo or staging primitives, and ad supply integrity answers distrust vendor-reported impressions.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers say claims are implied by combination and context and respond by restricting generation to a registry of approved claims, and semantic context layer answers say legitimate definitions conflict so the goal is forced disclosure of which definition was used rather than one true answer.
